newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 2.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

With yesterday nominated as the deadline for agreement by Tabcorp for a 164 percent increase in annual fee charges by Sky Channel for racing pictures, meetings between Tabcorp, Sky Channel and the racing industry continued well into last night in a bid toavert a Sky blackout of Victorian TAB agencies. Page 18.

North Sydney forward David Fairleigh has expressed bitter disappointment at his exclusion from the Australian rugby league side to tour Papua New Guinea. The Dally M second-rower of the year said last night he believed he would never play for Australia aain while the current panel of national selectors was in place. Page 18.

Both trainer Gai Waterhouse and jockey Kevin Forrester may continue business as usual pending the hearings of their appeals against charges and suspensions imposed by the Australian Jockey Club. Waterhouse had her licence to train suspended for three monhs and Forrester was suspended from riding for three months as a result of the Gossips inquiry. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Although he has neither the reputation nor the profile of some of his teammates, including Shane Heal, Isaac Burton and Melvin Thomas, personal statistics prove that basketballer Steve Whitehead will be a vital component of the Sydney Kings team when it mets the Canberra Cannons in the best-of-three National Basketball League quarter-finals series. Page 43.

Australian soccer coach Eddie Thomson has denied rumours that he held talks with leading Japanese officials about a role in the Japanese Soccer League. Thomson said he told Soccer Australia chairman David Hill nothing had happened to make him break his cntract, which will expire in 1998. Page 44.

Yesterday lodging an appeal over the three-match suspension of Michael Cheika, Randwick will wait until after the New South Wales Rugby Union appeals committee hears the case tonight, before naming a side for the grand final clash against Warringah. Page 44.
THE AGE

Injuring his back after a heavy fall during last Friday's loss to Adelaide, North Melbourne power forward Paul Maley is likely to be fit for this Friday's first National Basketball League quarter-final against South East Melbourne. Page C6.

Operation Payback will hand over power to an interim board headed by former president Ron Cook and including Don Scott, Ian Dicker and other key architects behind the rescue operation, as the board of the Hawthorn Football Club resigns today. Page C6.

On his debut at the seven-kilometre Belgian Grand Prix venue, young Australian international driver Mark Webber won a stunning victory in round two of the formula Ford Euro Cup at Spa yesterday. Page C6.
HERALD SUN

Richmond ruckman Justin Charles will spend his summer months playing baseball for Australian Baseball League team Melbourne Monarchs, but the AFL player must first recover from recent finger surgery to repair a sheath tendon. Page 77.

Australian tennis star Pat Rafter is concerned he won't be invited to play alongside Pete Sampras and Andre Agassi in the Colonial Classic at Kooyong in January, after splitting with his worldwide management company IMG, which is one of four partners in the tournament. Page 78.

Sydney Swans rookie Anthony Rocca has indicated he will nominate for the AFL pre-season draft if he is not traded, but, according to Rocca's manager Robert Conte, every club in Melbourne as well as Adelaide's Port Power had made inquiries about the 19-year-old. Page 80.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Parramatta forward Adam Ritson was released from intensive care at St Vincent's Private Hospital yesterday, after undergoing 14 operations on tumours on his brain. Forced to quit rugby league, Ritson's family hopes he will soon be released from hospital and enter a rehabilitation program. Page 70.

Since taking an American university scholarship and making his name on the U.S. tour, Australian golfer Steve Elkington has rarely played in Australia, but organisers of next month's A$1 million Australian Open in Sydney believe Elkington is a good chance to join Greg Norman and Tiger Woods in the tournament and the Greg Norman Classic at Royal Melbourne the following week. Page 70.

Trainer Jack Denham has hired Queensland's big occasion jockey Brian York to ride four-year-old Filante in Saturday's A$500,000 Canon Epsom Handicap at Randwick, in a move which could save bookmakers around Australia a multi-million dollar payout if he can win first place. Page 72.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2-373-1800
